ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (2024 revision, effective 1 January 2025); Administrative Measures for Beneficial Owner Information of Market Entities (People's Bank of China and State Administration for Market Regulation Order No. 3, effective 1 November 2024); Measures for the Administration of Enterprise Name Registration (SAMR Order No. 89, effective 1 March 2022); Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 revision, effective 1 July 2024); Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (effective 1 January 2020); for the Hong Kong investor parent, the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615) and the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Hong Kong investor company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hong Kong Notary Public certifies a true copy; the notarized certificate is then authenticated by China Legal Service (Hong Kong) Limited for use in the People's Republic of China. This is an intra-sovereign authentication channel distinct from and mutually exclusive with Hague Apostille and Consular Legalization; no apostille or consular legalization shall be applied.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Current Status of the Hong Kong investor company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hong Kong Companies Registry issues the certificate; a Hong Kong Notary Public notarizes a true copy; China Legal Service (Hong Kong) Limited authenticates the notarized copy for Mainland China use. This path replaces and excludes Hague Apostille and Consular Legalization because Hong Kong and Mainland China are within one sovereign state.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution of the Hong Kong investor company approving the establishment of the China WFOE and appointing the legal representative and authorized signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Hong Kong investor company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The board resolution is certified by the company secretary, notarized by a Hong Kong Notary Public, and authenticated by China Legal Service (Hong Kong) Limited. The notarized bundle must include the relevant extract of board minutes. No Hague Apostille and no Consular Legalization are required or permitted in this intra-China document path.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Memorandum and Articles) of the Hong Kong investor company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Hong Kong investor company as registered with the Hong Kong Companies Registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: A certified true copy of the registered Memorandum and Articles of Association is obtained from the Hong Kong Companies Registry, notarized by a Hong Kong Notary Public, and authenticated by China Legal Service (Hong Kong) Limited. This procedure is the exclusive intra-sovereign authentication route; Hague Apostille and Consular Legalization are mutually exclusive alternatives that shall not be chained here.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter / counterparty banking due diligence letter for the Hong Kong investor company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed bank in Hong Kong maintaining the investor's operational account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank letter is issued on bank letterhead and authenticated by an authorized bank officer; the letter is then notarized by a Hong Kong Notary Public and authenticated by China Legal Service (Hong Kong) Limited. The letter must be dated within 90 days of submission. This path does not involve Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization because the document originates in Hong Kong for use in Mainland China.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before filing, counsel must run a risk-based screening of every direct and indirect shareholder, beneficial owner, director, supervisor, senior manager, legal representative, and authorized signatory against the PBOC Beneficial Owner Information System and SAMR market entity database, the People's Bank of China money laundering risk list, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the OFAC Sectoral Sanctions Identifications List, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List including the 1267/1989 and 1988 sanctions regimes, and the UK and EU consolidated financial sanctions lists. Screening must include exact and fuzzy matching using alias, date of birth, nationality, passport number, and residential address cross-references; enhanced due diligence is mandatory for politically exposed persons and their immediate family or close associates. All screening results must be documented, signed by an independent compliance officer, and retained for at least five years. Any sanction hit triggers a hard stop and a reasoned legal memo before any registry filing, banking engagement, or name clearance is initiated.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Name Reservation and Registration System administered by the local Market Supervision Administration where the WFOE will be domiciled
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under SAMR Order No. 89, a mainland WFOE trade name must be constructed in four tiers: administrative division, distinctive trade name, industry or business scope description, and legal form. The Chinese name is mandatory for all registration, tax, and bank account documents. An English name may be registered as a secondary name on the business license only if it is a phonetic or semantic transliteration of the registered Chinese trade name and is not inconsistent or confusingly similar to the Chinese name. No Latin letters, Arabic digits, or special characters are permitted in the Chinese name unless special approval is obtained; the administrative division and legal form tiers must be pure Chinese ideographs.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant should first obtain the written decision and the statutory reason from the local Market Supervision Administration. Within sixty days of receiving the rejection, the applicant may file an administrative reconsideration application with the next higher Market Supervision Administration under the Administrative Reconsideration Law, or alternatively file an administrative lawsuit with the competent Basic People's Court within six months. The reconsideration application must include the original name application record, the proposed revised name, a legal memorandum distinguishing any cited prior right or prohibited token, and any consent letter from an earlier registrant if the rejection was based on name similarity. The higher authority must issue a decision within sixty days of acceptance, and that decision may itself be challenged in court.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices and commercial mailboxes are not permissible for a mainland China WFOE engaged in generative AI and LLM API operations. The PRC Company Law and the Market Entity Registration Regulations require a fixed physical address at the time of establishment. The tax authority and the bank will reject a virtual office or PO box because the three-in-one business license application and corporate account opening require a lease contract, property ownership certificate, landlord identity, or sublease consent plus on-site verification. An ISIC 6201 or NAICS 541511 business needs physical servers, personnel, cloud contracts, and business records to demonstrate effective management and commercial substance; a virtual mailbox will trigger rejection of VAT invoice issuance, denial of bank account opening, and deregistration action for off-site presence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) business license hung at the letterbox; (2) staff present during working hours; (3) lease deed matching the registered address; (4) utility bills in the WFOE name; (5) computers, servers, or cloud contract evidence supporting the AI/LLM business; (6) accounting and corporate records maintained at the address; (7) company name plate displayed; (8) landlord property ownership certificate or sublease authorization. Quantified risk of unannounced physical inspection by municipal tax or SAMR authorities within the first twelve months: High (70-80%) if the registered address is a shared office, virtual mailbox, or cluster address; Moderate (30-40%) for a directly leased solo office in an ordinary commercial building; Low (10-15%) for a leased grade-A office with visible staff and dedicated equipment. Noncompliance with any checklist item triggers an order to correct, administrative penalty, or revocation of the business license.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) / local Market Supervision Administration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory official fee; company registration and name pre-approval are free of charge in all provinces

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and authentication of Hong Kong investor documents (five instruments: incorporation certificate, good standing, board resolution, articles, bank reference letter)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Hong Kong Notary Public and China Legal Service (Hong Kong) Limited
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market tariff of HKD 7,000-9,000 notary fee plus China Legal Service authentication fee, converted at approximately 7.8 HKD per USD

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: SAMR-accredited translation agency or notary translation service
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of RMB 150-250 per page plus certification stamp

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Public security bureau-approved seal engraving vendor
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark; variable by provincial public security fee schedule

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622), Laws of Hong Kong SAR, principally the provisions on incorporation by registration (Part 2), share capital allotment and returns (Part 4), powers of directors (Part 13), registered office and corporate records (Part 16), and annual statutory returns (Part 17), together with the Companies (Fees and Charges) Regulation
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies Registry, Hong Kong SAR, operating through the e-Registry online portal (www.eregistry.gov.hk) and the one-stop company and business registration arrangement with the Inland Revenue Department
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Form NNC1 (Incorporation Form for Company Limited by Shares), delivered with the Articles of Association and the Notice to Business Registration Office IRBR1
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Hong Kong law prescribes no minimum paid-up capital for a company limited by shares; the WFOE may be incorporated with one issued ordinary share of HKD 1.00 or such nominal value as stated in its Articles of Association. No blocked escrow account is required. However, where the WFOE needs bank account opening or investor due diligence, the first board resolution will authorize the subscriber to pay up the allotted shares in cash, and the bank or Companies Registry may require a bank certificate or source-of-funds declaration for the paid-up capital
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF CN HK WFOE LIMITED (THE COMPANY), PASSED BY THE SUBSCRIBER, THE SOLE DIRECTOR AND THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE COMPANIES ORDINANCE (CAP. 622) AND THE COMPANY'S ARTICLES OF ASSOCIATION. 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: RESOLVED that the subscriber, CN PARENT CORPORATION or its lawful assignee, be and is hereby allotted and issued one thousand ordinary shares of HKD 1.00 each at par, credited as fully paid upon realization of the subscription funds into the Company's bank account, and that the directors be and are hereby authorized to file all allotment returns, pay the prescribed fees, and obtain the bank receipt certifying the paid-up capital. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: RESOLVED that the directors be and are hereby authorized to open and maintain corporate current accounts and, where appropriate, digital asset and multi-currency settlement accounts with one or more licensed banks or authorized payment service providers in Hong Kong SAR, to appoint two authorized signatories to act jointly for any transaction above HKD 50,000, and to provide each financial institution with certified copies of this resolution, the Certificate of Incorporation, the Business Registration Certificate, the Articles of Association, and the beneficial ownership declaration for anti-money-laundering compliance. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company be and is hereby adopted at the address of the licensed corporate service provider in Hong Kong SAR, namely [ADDRESS OF REGISTERED OFFICE], and that the directors be and are hereby authorized to deliver Form NR1 to the Companies Registry if the registered office is later changed. 4. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS: RESOLVED that [NAME OF FIRST DIRECTOR] be and is hereby appointed as the first director of the Company, [NAME OF COMPANY SECRETARY FIRM OR INDIVIDUAL] be and is hereby appointed as company secretary of the Company, and [NAME OF AUDITOR FIRM] be and is hereby appointed as the first auditor of the Company, each appointment to take effect forthwith and continue until the next annual general meeting. 5. GENERAL AUTHORITY: RESOLVED that the directors be and are hereby authorized to apply for the Business Registration Certificate, to open mandatory provident fund arrangements, to execute leases and service agreements, to engage legal counsel and tax advisers, and to take all steps necessary to register the Company for corporate tax and, if required, value-added tax or digital services tax in any jurisdiction where the Company transacts business. 6. RATIFICATION: RESOLVED that all acts previously or concurrently done by the subscriber and the directors in connection with the incorporation of the Company, including the payment of incorporation fees and the preparation of statutory books, be and are hereby ratified, confirmed and adopted as the Company's own actions. THIS RESOLUTION IS EFFECTIVE IMMEDIATELY AND MAY BE SIGNED IN COUNTERPARTS.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company name search and pre-incorporation structural documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry, Hong Kong SAR — electronic Company Name Search via e-Registry; Hong Kong Trade Marks Registry for trademark conflict checks
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a Companies Registry name search through the e-Registry portal and a Trade Marks Registry search to confirm that the proposed English name ending in Limited and any optional Chinese name are not identical, deceptively similar, or conflicting with existing marks. Verify that the registered office address is physically in Hong Kong SAR and that the landlord or corporate service provider has consented to use. Prepare the Memorandum and Articles of Association, the beneficial ownership and AML/CFT file for the subscriber, and draft the intended principal business description for ISIC 6201, namely the provision of generative artificial intelligence and large language model inference API services. Obtain certified passports, proof of residential address, professional references if required, and signed consent from the first director, company secretary and auditor.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and name search certificate or reference number
Draft Articles of Association and subscriber statement
Certified passport and proof of residential address of subscriber, director and beneficial owner
Consent letter of landlord or corporate service provider for registered office
AML/CFT due-diligence file and identification details of ultimate beneficial owner
Draft business scope description for ISIC 6201 and NAICS 541511
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Registry notifies that the proposed name is unavailable or deceptively similar, the applicant shall file a revised name through the same portal on the same day; the Registrar does not refund the name search fee, and the incorporation application will be resubmitted under the corrected name. If a trademark conflict is identified, the submission must be withdrawn and the name changed before incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic incorporation filing and payment of statutory fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry e-Registry — One-stop Company and Business Registration portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log on to the Companies Registry e-Registry and select the one-stop company and business registration service. Complete and digitally execute Form NNC1, attach the Articles of Association, and submit the Notice to Business Registration Office IRBR1 in one package. Insert the full particulars of the subscriber, first director, company secretary, registered office and intended business description, then validate all fields against the consent letters. Pay the Companies Registry incorporation fee of HKD 1,720 and the Business Registration fee and levy of HKD 2,150 by licensed electronic payment, retain the payment receipt, and note the application reference. The Registrar will examine the documents for statutory compliance, including the name availability check and the statement of compliance, and upon successful registration will issue the Certificate of Incorporation and the Business Registration Certificate.
required_dossiers: Form NNC1 duly completed and digitally signed
Articles of Association marked as the company constitution
Notice to Business Registration Office IRBR1
Subscriber consent and designated digital signature authority
Payment receipt for Companies Registry and Business Registration fees
Security check or acknowledgment from the corporate service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a requisition or query after submission, the corporate service provider must respond within fourteen days using the online requisition-reply function, submitting corrected NNC1 or Articls pages and any requested supporting declaration. If registration is suspended, the applicant may withdraw and resubmit after curing the defect, provided the same name is still available, or appeal to the Registrar in writing with a statutory declaration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business registration and Inland Revenue Department notification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Business Registration Office, Hong Kong SAR
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Companies Registry approves incorporation, confirm that the Business Registration Certificate has been issued automatically under the one-stop arrangement. If the certificate is not received online within one business day, file the Business Registration application or requisition with the Business Registration Office and attach the Certificate of Incorporation and the IRBR1 acknowledgment. Certify that the business description accurately covers software development, information technology consultancy and the provision of generative AI and LLM API platform services. Obtain the Business Registration number and display the certificate at the registered office as required. If the Inland Revenue Department queries the nature of business, submit within fourteen days the tenancy agreement, the shareholder's certificate of incorporation or passport, and a one-page business plan describing the AI API revenue model and expected payment rails.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Companies Registry
Incorporation Form NNC1 and IRBR1 acknowledgment
Proof of registered office address and landlord consent
Business description certificate or board statement for ISIC 6201
Identity and address proof of the designated tax representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Business Registration Certificate is denied or queried, the WFOE must submit a corrected IRBR1 together with a cover letter to the Business Registration Office and provide a revised principal business activity description. Any late or non-registration penalty can be mitigated by showing good faith reliance on the one-stop service, but the prudent remedy is immediate rectification before any assessment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First board meeting, share allotment return and bank account activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry (return of allotment) and Hong Kong Monetary Authority licensed authorized institution or licensed payment processor
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the statutory first board meeting or execute a unanimous written resolution adopting the pro-forma first board resolution in the Company's statutory minute book. Allot the subscribed shares to the shareholder and receive the paid-up capital in the Company's bank account, then file Form NSC1 with the Companies Registry within one month of allotment and pay the prescribed filing fee. Deliver to the chosen licensed bank or financial institution the certified board resolution, Certificate of Incorporation, Business Registration Certificate, Articles of Association, register of directors and beneficial ownership declaration. Complete the AML/KYC forms and disclose the intended settlement rails, including Stripe and USDC, and the anticipated monthly transaction volumes for the LLM API platform. The bank must verify source of funds for the paid-up capital before issuing the account opening confirmation.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the first board resolution
Form NSC1 Return of Allotment and Companies Registry fee receipt
Certificate of Incorporation and Business Registration Certificate
Register of directors, company secretary and beneficial owners
Bank account opening application, AML/KYC forms and source-of-funds evidence
Completed customer risk assessment for AI API token payment business
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Registry rejects Form NSC1 because of missing signatures or incorrect allotment date, the company must correct and refile within the balance of the prescribed period or, if late, pay the late filing penalty and submit a covering statutory declaration explaining the oversight. If the bank refuses the account application due to enhanced due diligence, the directors should provide an independent legal opinion on licensing exemptions and a detailed transaction-flow diagram, or apply to a tier-two licensed bank in Hong Kong SAR.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory registers, mandatory provident fund and post-incorporation compliance notification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry, Mandatory Provident Fund Schemes Authority, and Inland Revenue Department as applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Maintain the statutory books at the registered office or at the corporate service provider, including the register of members, register of directors and secretaries, register of charges, and records of resolutions and minutes. File any required notification of appointment of company secretary with the Companies Registry and, if the initial registered office or director details differ from the incorporation application, file the corresponding change form. If the WFOE will employ Hong Kong staff, register with the Mandatory Provident Fund Schemes Authority and enroll employees in an approved MPF scheme within the statutory deadline. Notify the Inland Revenue Department and the Companies Registry of any later changes to business name, physical office, business description, or banking details. For any leased office, obtain a valid fire safety verification from the landlord or the Fire Services Department for the premises, while preserving the digital-only characterization of the AI API business.
required_dossiers: Statutory registers and index of documents
Company secretary appointment form and consent
MPF scheme employer registration and employee enrolment forms
Lease agreement and landlord fire safety confirmation
Registered office service agreement with corporate service provider
Annual return and profits tax election calendar prepared by counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any post-incorporation notification is rejected or returned, the responsible director should amend the form with the correct company number and particulars and resubmit within the statutory cure period. If a filing deadline has passed, the company should file a late-fee application with a written explanation to the Companies Registry and retain the acknowledgment to mitigate civil penalties.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable — the entity operates under ISIC 6201 as a generative artificial intelligence and LLM API platform, which is a digital information technology service, not a physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly or warehousing activity

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable — no full Environmental Impact Assessment, environmental registration or discharge permit is required for a pure digital service company; the WFOE will not own or operate any industrial plant
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable — the WFOE generates no industrial wastewater, volatile organic compound emissions or hazardous waste; the only environmental obligations are general office waste segregation, electrical safety, and landlord’s building management rules for the leased office premises

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable as an industrial or civil-defense operating permit; however, the Hong Kong SAR office must comply with the Fire Services (Installations and Equipment) Regulations (Cap. 95F) and the Occupational Safety and Health Ordinance (Cap. 509) before occupation, and the landlord or building owner must provide fire safety verification for the leased premises, including emergency exit routes and portable fire extinguishers, where the WFOE maintains its administrative and engineering team

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China, acting through the local tax service bureau in the WFOE's registered place; electronic filing through the STA's Electronic Tax Bureau (ETB/electronic tax filing portal) at www.chinatax.gov.cn.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: On incorporation, the WFOE obtains a Business License from the Market Regulation Administration bearing the 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which automatically constitutes the PRC Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) and VAT registration number. Within 30 days after the Business License is issued, the WFOE must complete supplementary tax registration ('tax information collection') in the Electronic Tax Bureau, uploading the Business License, Articles of Association, Hong Kong shareholder's Certificate of Incorporation and Business Registration certificate, director/legal representative identification documents, registered office lease/property title, basic bank account opening certificate, and appointment of financial/accounting personnel. The ETB then activates the tax types, assigns the entity's VAT taxpayer status (small-scale or general VAT taxpayer), and issues an electronic tax registration record. A foreign non-resident entity (for example, a Hong Kong parent) that has no separate PRC establishment does not need a domestic TIN merely to own the WFOE; however, if it independently earns PRC-source income or engages in taxable PRC activities, it must apply to the competent tax bureau for a non-resident enterprise tax number by submitting its Hong Kong incorporation and Business Registration documents, the relevant income contract, and a PRC tax representative appointment, after which the STA assigns a non-resident TIN for withholding tax and reporting purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - the CN WFOE is a PRC resident limited liability company taxed at entity level, subject to Enterprise Income Tax at 25% on worldwide income and VAT on taxable turnover; it is not pass-through eligible.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for entity classification; PRC tax law does not provide a check-the-box election or hybrid-mismatch entity election. Under VAT, a small-scale taxpayer may voluntarily register as a general VAT taxpayer, and certain small-scale taxpayers may elect simplified taxation; general VAT taxpayer status becomes mandatory once annual taxable sales exceed the statutory threshold.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the VAT Law of the People's Republic of China. The PRC headline standard VAT rate is 13%; the applicable rate for AI/LLM API platform services, classified as modern services / software and information technology services, is 6%; cross-border zero-rated exports are taxed at 0%.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: All PRC legal-person companies must complete VAT registration upon business-license issuance. Mandatory general VAT taxpayer registration arises when cumulative annual taxable sales exceed CNY 5,000,000. Below that threshold, the entity remains a small-scale taxpayer; monthly taxable sales up to CNY 100,000 are currently exempt from VAT under the applicable small-scale taxpayer concession.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The WFOE must issue VAT invoices through the State Taxation Administration's Electronic Invoice Service Platform. Full digital electronic invoices (FDEI) are generated and transmitted to the STA's Golden Tax Phase IV system in real time; each invoice carries a digital anti-counterfeiting QR code and tax classification code. General VAT taxpayers must use tax-control UKey software, integrate ERP/accounting systems through the ETB's API reporting interface, and submit invoice data for automatic reconciliation with VAT returns, bank payment flows and customs declarations. There is no physical fiscal stamp for FDEIs; tax clearance is achieved through real-time digital invoice validation in the ETB.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Cross-border AI/LLM API platform services qualify for 0% VAT zero-rating if: (1) the services are supplied by the PRC WFOE to an overseas non-resident customer; (2) the services are wholly consumed outside mainland China; (3) the service falls within the statutory zero-rated cross-border software services / information system services / business process management services / offshore outsourcing categories; and (4) the taxpayer has completed the one-time cross-border taxable services zero-rating/exemption recordation in the Electronic Tax Bureau and retains supporting evidence. Physical export of goods containing or reproducing software is zero-rated upon electronic export declaration and customs release under the export tax rebate system. The WFOE may claim input VAT refund/credit attributable to zero-rated export supplies only to the extent the zero-rating is substantiated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Goods Declaration / Bill of Entry issued by China Customs with export customs release code
Signed Bill of Lading (sea), Air Waybill (air) or courier export proof (for physical goods or media containing software)
Export sales contract and commercial invoice identifying the overseas buyer and stating that the AI/LLM API service or software is supplied from the PRC
Bank-issued foreign exchange receipt voucher / Cross-Border Income Declaration / Inward Remittance Certificate evidencing payment received from the overseas customer
Electronic Tax Bureau recordation certificate confirming cross-border taxable services zero-rating or exemption

Service delivery and consumption evidence, including API token usage logs, server access records, system management reports, or an overseas customer attestation confirming no mainland China consumption
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: STA tax risk teams under the Golden Tax Phase IV system will match zero-rated VAT filings with customs electronic declarations, bank foreign-exchange receipts and service consumption evidence. If zero-rating is not substantiated, the tax authority recovers output VAT at the applicable rate (6% for AI/LLM API services, 13% for goods) plus a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% of the unpaid tax, and may impose an administrative penalty of 50% to five times the underpaid or over-refunded tax under the PRC Tax Collection and Administration Law. Falsifying export documents, using forged Inward Remittance Certificates, or fraudulently claiming export refunds can trigger criminal liability for fraudulent export tax refunds (Criminal Law Article 204) and issuance of false special VAT invoices (Criminal Law Article 205), with imprisonment and criminal fines for responsible individuals.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC); delegated to the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) for all foreign exchange administration
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China operates a managed floating RMB regime with asymmetric convertibility. Current account items are substantially liberalised: export receipts can be retained in foreign currency or settled into RMB, import and service payments are processed by designated banks against underlying contracts, invoices and customs declarations, and after-tax profits may be remitted to overseas shareholders once the bank verifies audited financials, tax payment stamps and the board resolution. Capital account items remain tightly controlled. A wholly foreign-owned enterprise cannot freely convert equity capital into RMB for prohibited uses; SAFE registration, a dedicated FDI capital account, and post-circulation monitoring are required. Equity injections may not be used to on-lend funds to related parties, to purchase domestic securities without authorisation, or to pay for assets unrelated to the declared business scope. Because the parent is a Hong Kong entity, the WFOE must demonstrate that the HK investor is the genuine ultimate beneficiary, that inbound wires have proper FDI purpose codes, and that any dividend outflow matches after-tax distributable profits. In practice, banks apply authenticity testing on every current-account remittance; any non-genuine or circular flow is declined. Convertibility therefore exists for real business transactions but not as a right for arbitrary capital flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: China no longer imposes a fixed mandatory export surrender ratio. Under the current trade FX administration framework administered through SAFE's 'ASOne' trade monitoring system, export proceeds must be repatriated directly into a domestic corporate foreign exchange settlement account and must arrive by the contractual payment date agreed with the overseas buyer; where the contract does not define a date, banks conventionally treat 90 days after customs declaration or service completion as the statutory collection benchmark. Upon receipt, the WFOE may keep the foreign currency balance, or sell it to the bank for RMB at the market rate. The bank will require an export declaration matched with an invoice, a bill of lading or electronic service confirmation, and a balance of payments indirect reporting entry; only then are the funds released for use. There is no permissible channel for keeping export proceeds offshore without registration.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI Foreign Exchange Capital Account (Capital Escrow Account)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: RMB Basic Deposit Account with Multi-Currency Settlement
Basic Operational Currency Account (CNY General Settlement Account)
Foreign Exchange Settlement Account for Export Proceeds

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to nil for onshore China. PBOC and SAFE prohibit unlicensed non-bank institutions from opening domestic RMB accounts or performing foreign exchange settlement for corporate entities. Offshore EMIs such as Wise, Revolut, Payoneer, or Airwallex cannot provide a lawful CNY clearing account for a China-domiciled WFOE, but may be used at the Hong Kong treasury level only if the entity maintains a Hong Kong subsidiary outside this WFOE. An FDI capital injection cannot be routed through an EMI; inbound funds must enter via a licensed domestic bank with SAFE registration. Any recommended architecture must keep the WFOE's CNY treasury fully inside China.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The PRC legal representative or a China-resident senior officer holding an authorized letter of attorney must visit the branch in person to complete account opening. Remote consular proxy account opening is not permitted as the sole mechanism; HK-sourced documents must be notarised by a China-appointed notary, and the bank will conduct a video KYC call with all 25%-and-above ultimate beneficial owners. Original company chop (seal) and board resolutions must be produced at the physical visit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership is obscured by a Hong Kong corporate parent with nominee shareholders or a shelf company structure; bank cannot natural-person-verify the true controller.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Combined dossier: Hong Kong Companies Registry current extracts and annual returns; certificate of incorporation; memorandum and articles; full shareholder registry from HK to ultimate natural person; passport and proof-of-address for each natural person holding 25% or more; beneficial ownership declaration signed under HK Companies Ordinance; group structure chart with ownership percentages; Chinese versions of above notarised by a China-appointed Notary Public in Hong Kong and authenticated for PRC bank use.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection is scheduled from a Hong Kong parent whose financial capacity is unproven or whose account shows rapid round-tripping, commingled client funds, or deposit-and-withdraw patterns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The HK parent's audited financial statements for the last three years; bank statements covering the preceding 12 months; source-of-wealth statement for the injection amount; board resolution and minutes approving the investment; undertaking letter that funds are not borrowed from third parties or derived from illegal activities; if the HK parent itself receives group funding, present the group funding agreement and downstream contribution schedule; followed by SAFE FDI registration certificate and the bank's FX business registration voucher.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border service revenue from LLM API sales is intangible, high-volume, and hard to evidence as genuinely trade-related; bank fears the WFOE is being used for invoice manipulation or disguised capital flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master service or SaaS agreement executed between the WFOE and each material customer; current-generation API usage and token consumption reports from underlying cloud/intelligence platforms; third-party bandwidth and hosting invoices; periodic billing and payment reconciliation ledgers; VAT e-invoices or tax payment certificates; software copyright registration for the proprietary models; BOP service-trade filing forms and a written transfer-pricing narrative showing arm's-length royalties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The target payment rail includes USDC cryptocurrency; Chinese regulators prohibit virtual-currency settlement and banks must screen for crypto-derived proceeds entering China.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PRC legal opinion confirming that the onshore WFOE will not accept or send USDC; written treasury policy restricting all onshore customer payments to bank transfers, MT103 and LC rails; subsidiary intercompany agreement with any Hong Kong treasury vehicle showing that USDC, if any, stops at the HK ring-fenced wallet and never crosses into the China banking system; bank compliance training certificates for staff; transaction-level audit trail and attestation that all WFOE invoices are settled through licensed banking channels.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Before drawing down equity, the WFOE obtains a SAFE FDI foreign exchange registration certificate and opens a dedicated foreign-exchange capital account at a domestic tier-1 bank. The HK parent sends a SWIFT MT103 quoting the beneficiary account, the SAFE FDI purpose code for equity injection, and the WFOE's unified social credit code. The receiving bank matches the inward payment notice to the SAFE registration and credits the capital account. If converting into RMB, the WFOE submits the capital account payment or usage declaration under the Circular 19 framework, listing payroll, rent, procurement or R&D expenses; the bank releases RMB only against those permitted items. Within six months of contribution, a PRC certified public accountant issues a capital verification report and the WFOE updates its business registration; the bank closes the foreign exchange filing after the contribution is confirmed.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For AI API platform disbursements, recurring supplier payments use SWIFT MT103 with an underlying contract and invoice. Commercial letters of credit and documentary collections are accepted where a banker's undertaking is needed for procurement of hardware or server equipment under documentary compliance. Digital service payments should not be forced into LC; the bank will process MT103 service remittances under SAFE current-account authenticity verification. For payments to the HK parent, covering profit repatriation, service fees or IP royalties, the bank requires withholding tax certificates, audited profit records, tax-bureau contract registration, board approval, and proper BOP reporting before release.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards between CNY and USD/HKD for committed cash flows arising from equity capital deployment, software licensing fees and dividend repatriation; subject to underlying exposure documentation and bank's bilateral ISDA or master agreement
FX swaps, both same-day and dated, to manage temporary liquidity mismatches between CNY settlement balances and foreign-currency receivables or payables
Plain-vanilla FX options, call or put, for contingency hedging of AI API pricing exposure, permitted only for hedging and not for proprietary speculation
Cross-currency swaps for long-term USD/CNY exposures linked to offshore compute infrastructure leases or external loans, provided the WFOE documents debt or trade service background

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permissible as an onshore treasury instrument for the China WFOE; such instruments may only be used by the Hong Kong treasury vehicle for CNH and are expressly outside the WFOE's SAFE-registered books

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (NAR1) for a Hong Kong private company limited by shares
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies Registry, Hong Kong SAR Government
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after each anniversary of the date of incorporation, using the registered particulars as at that anniversary date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fees are HK$1,200 if the return is filed more than 42 days but not more than 3 months late; HK$2,400 if more than 3 months but not more than 6 months late; HK$3,600 if more than 6 months but not more than 12 months late; and HK$4,800 if more than 12 months late. Continued non-filing is a statutory offence, directors are liable to prosecution, and the Registrar may initiate administrative strike-off under section 746 of the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) after formal correspondence, publication in the Gazette, and expiry of the objection period.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Business Registration Certificate renewal under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), Business Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month before the expiry of the existing Business Registration Certificate; the certificate is normally renewed annually and the IRD issues a renewal demand one month before expiry.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Carrying on business without a valid Business Registration Certificate is an offence, punishable on conviction by a fine of HK$5,000 and imprisonment for one year, plus a daily fine of HK$50 for continuing offences without reasonable excuse. Failure to renew may also be treated by the Companies Registry as evidence that the company is not carrying on business and may support administrative strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profits Tax Return (BIR51) together with audited financial statements and tax computation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ordinarily not later than one month from the date of issue of BIR51; under the IRD block extension scheme, when a tax representative is appointed for an accounting period ending on a common date such as 31 December, the filing deadline is routinely extended to a later date (commonly August or November depending on the year of assessment).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The IRD may make an estimated assessment based on available information. Without reasonable excuse, failure to file a return when required is an offence punishable by a fine at Level 3 (HK$10,000) plus a further fine of treble the amount of tax undercharged. Unpaid tax also attracts a 5% late-payment surcharge after 6 months and an additional 5% surcharge after a further 6 months, after which the IRD may commence distraint or court collection proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer's Return (BIR56A and related BIR56B schedules for employees, directors, and former staff)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Not later than one month after the issue date of the return form; for the usual year of assessment ended 31 December, the return is normally issued on 1 April and is due by 1 May.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-submission is an offence under the Inland Revenue Ordinance; the maximum penalty is a Level 3 fine (HK$10,000) and treble the amount of tax undercharged. Continued non-compliance may trigger estimated employer assessments, personal liability for directors, and IRD debt-collection enforcement.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No quantitative de minimis threshold applies in Hong Kong. Every company incorporated under the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) that is not dormant must appoint a Hong Kong certified public accountant as auditor and cause its financial statements to be audited annually, regardless of turnover, total assets, revenue, profit, or employee headcount. The only available exemption is for a dormant private company that has no significant accounting transactions and follows the statutory dormant-company procedure. A generative AI and LLM API platform with any trading revenue, active bank activity, USDC or other cryptocurrency receipts, or employee compensation is an active company and is therefore subject to a mandatory statutory audit by a licensed CPA for every financial year.

stage_5.governing_accounting_framework: Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622); Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS) issued by the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants (HKICPA), which are substantially converged with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS); eligible private companies may apply HKFRS for Private Entities, which is the Hong Kong equivalent of the IFRS for SMEs framework. No separate local non-HKFRS GAAP is available to an active Hong Kong company.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Hong Kong does not impose an annual UBO confirmation filing to the Companies Registry. Instead, each company must maintain a Significant Controllers Register at its registered office or a prescribed location; the register must be updated within 7 days of any change in a significant controller and must be available for inspection by Hong Kong law enforcement authorities without an annual public filing. There is no 30-day corporate-register filing window for shareholding transfers, but a share transfer instrument executed in Hong Kong must be presented to the Inland Revenue Department for stamp duty within 30 days of execution or the instrument becomes inadmissible in evidence and penalties may apply. The NAR1 annual return separately delivers the current register of members, share capital, directors, company secretary, and registered office particulars at the anniversary date; this return is not a UBO declaration and does not publicly disclose beneficial owners.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Company Secretaries
Minute Book (shareholder meetings, director meetings, and written resolutions)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 200 - USD 1,000 per annum for a standard Hong Kong registered office and company secretarial agent service
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 - USD 9,000 per annum for a single-entity AI/LLM API platform with moderate transaction volume and HKFRS-compliant audited financial statements; the range may increase if consolidated group statutory audits or complex USDC/cryptocurrency financial instruments are present.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law, Article 4); 15% preferential rate available only for qualified High and New Technology Enterprises or encouraged software/IC enterprises.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualified AI WFOE may claim: 15% HNTE reduced rate; 100% super deduction of eligible R&D expenses (Article 30 and MOF/SAT 2023 Announcement); integrated circuit/software enterprise two-year exemption plus three-year 50% reduction; no automatic free-zone holiday for ordinary WFOE.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Enterprise Income Tax Return of the People's Republic of China (Form A05001, main form A100000, with supplemental schedules) filed through the State Taxation Administration's electronic tax filing portal (eTax system).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual settlement within five months after fiscal year-end; quarterly provisional returns on the 15th day after each quarter-end.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual return and payment due on or before May 31 of the calendar year immediately following the fiscal year-end; quarterly provisional payment due by the 15th day of the fourth month following the close of each quarter.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from sale of goods, provision of AI inference services, API token consumption, custom model licensing, and related operating income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recognize revenue at the WFOE as the China-resident seller; do not net out intercompany platform fees. Cross-border cloud costs are deductible only if supported by contracts, service substance evidence, and valid VAT invoices; otherwise a transfer-pricing adjustment is required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs of rendering AI/LLM services, including GPU cloud capacity, data storage, bandwidth, salaries of engineers, and amortization of intangible assets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Charges from Hong Kong affiliates must be at arm's length and economically beneficial to the WFOE. Absence of benefit test triggers disallowance. Ensure services are not double-deducted under cost-sharing or mark-up arrangements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 / Lines 103-110 (Taxes and Surcharges on Operations)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enterprise income tax paid on quarterly provisional returns, VAT, consumption tax, city maintenance and construction tax, education surcharges, property tax, and land use tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: VAT on cross-border royalties collected on behalf of non-resident vendors is allowed as a credit only if valid special VAT invoices are obtained; do not include self-assessed withholding income tax in deductible taxes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 / Lines 111-133 (Administrative, Selling, and Financial Expenses)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Management service fees, royalties, interest on related-party debt, marketing expenses, and bank charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Royalties paid to the Hong Kong parent require economic substance at the recipient and an arm's-length royalty rate. Interest on thin-capitalized intercompany loans exceeding the 2:1 debt-to-equity safe harbor is non-deductible and may be reclassified as a deemed dividend subject to withholding tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 / Lines 141-155 (Non-Operating Income and Gains on Disposal of Assets)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disposal gains, government subsidies not otherwise excluded, exchange gains, and other non-operating income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include gains on disposal of China-source intangible assets to non-residents as Chinese-source income; for offshore-to-offshore sale of a China resident entity's shares, apply SAT anti-avoidance rules requiring withholding and contemporaneous reporting.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting net profit before tax under the PRC Accounting Standards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the WFOE receives a dividend from a Hong Kong subsidiary, the dividend is foreign-source income but remains taxable at 25% unless foreign tax credit rules under Article 23 apply; dividends paid by the WFOE to the Hong Kong parent are separately subject to withholding tax on the distribution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation between accounting profit and taxable income; includes transfer-pricing adjustments, thin-capitalization add-backs, entertainment disallowances, and tax-exempt income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare intercompany transactions in Schedule G100000; attach contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation when thresholds are met. Any payment to a Hong Kong associate lacking economic substance must be added back.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 / Line 201 (Taxable Income after Loss Carryforwards)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after deducting allowable carryforward losses from prior years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss carryforward is generally five years; integrated circuit enterprises and high-tech enterprises may enjoy longer periods only if qualified. Do not use Hong Kong losses against WFOE profits without China branch/loss allocation compliance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 9 / Lines 202-219 (Tax Credits and Preferential Tax Reductions)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: HNTE 15% rate, R&D super-deduction, foreign tax credit, venture capital/equipment credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For dividends paid by WFOE to Hong Kong parent, tax credits do not reduce withholding tax; withholding is a separate obligation of the payer. The benefit holder must be the true economic owner to invoke treaty relief.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax payable after quarterly provisional payments, representing the settlement amount due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Before remitting any dividend, calculate the statutory 10% non-resident withholding on the entire distribution, then examine whether the 5% Mainland-Hong Kong DTA rate applies; withhold and pay the resulting amount within seven days of the payment date, or as prescribed by the withholding return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment triggers a daily surcharge of 0.05% on the unpaid tax for each day of delay under the Tax Collection Administration Law Article 32. Failure to file returns is penalized under Article 62 with a fine up to RMB 2,000, or RMB 2,000-10,000 for serious cases. False or fraudulent filing constitutes tax evasion under Article 63: recovery of unpaid tax, surcharge, and a penalty from 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax; criminal tax evasion under PRC Criminal Law Articles 201 and 211 can lead to imprisonment up to seven years and fines.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory withholding for dividends paid by a Chinese WFOE to a non-resident enterprise (EIT Law Articles 3, 27, 37); reduced to 5% under the Mainland-Hong Kong Double Taxation Arrangement where the beneficial owner is a Hong Kong company directly holding at least 25% of the WFOE's capital for 12 months before the dividend is declared.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The HK parent must obtain a Hong Kong Tax Residency Certificate covering the entitlement year, submit a completed beneficial ownership self-attestation form, evidence the 12-month 25% direct holding chain, and provide board minutes and audited accounts showing it is not a pass-through. The WFOE files the withholding return with the Chinese SAT before remittance, attaches the treaty claim and supporting documents; if the claim is accepted, withholding is reduced from 10% to 5% and the excess already withheld is refundable or creditable only through adjustment. Failure to prove substance or a merely formal construction invites denial under the Principal Purpose Test of the Arrangement and the general anti-avoidance rule.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on gross interest and royalties paid to non-residents is 10% each. Under the Mainland-Hong Kong Arrangement, interest and royalty payments beneficially owned by a Hong Kong resident are taxed at 7%, unless the Hong Kong taxpayer is also the registered/beneficial owner of the patent/software and the IP is developed in Hong Kong. VAT and surcharges may also apply on royalty/licence fees; the withholding agent must separately report enterprise income tax and VAT.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File threshold: controlled tangible-asset transfers above RMB 200 million, financial-asset transfers above RMB 100 million, intangible-asset transfers above RMB 100 million, and other related-party transactions above RMB 40 million. Master File threshold: aggregate related-party revenue/expenses above RMB 1 billion. Annual related-party transaction reporting (Schedule G100000) is required regardless of amount, and contemporaneous documentation must be prepared by the filing date.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China applies substance-over-form through the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (EIT Law Article 47) and special tax adjustments; a WFOE must have real personnel, servers/license assets, and management functions in China. For Hong Kong, the Economic Substance Regulations require entities claiming Hong Kong tax benefits and DTA access to demonstrate Core Income-Generating Activities in Hong Kong; a functional, IT, or financing entity must have adequate CIGA, premises, and employees. Failure to prove substance denies treaty benefits and may create employment/WFOE permanent-establishment exposure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Invoicing (Artificial Inflation of Deductions)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE creates or purchases forged value-added-tax invoices for fake cloud/AI consulting services from third parties or related Hong Kong vendors, artificially increasing deductible expenses and reducing taxable profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax Collection Administration Law Article 63 imposes recovery of unpaid tax, a daily surcharge of 0.05%, and a monetary penalty of 50%-500% of the underpaid tax; Criminal Law Articles 205 and 210 subject the issuer and user of false special VAT invoices to criminal fines and imprisonment, with aggravated penalties for large-scale invoice fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve the false invoices or sign fraudulent returns can be held solidarily liable for unpaid corporate taxes where the corporate veil is pierced for abuse of corporate personality; tax authorities may impose exit restrictions/travel bans under Article 44, and individual prosecutors may pursue criminal liability leading to imprisonment up to seven years for tax evasion and asset forfeiture/restitution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Treaty Shopping and Shell Company Abuse (Improper DTA Claim)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Hong Kong parent is a shell company without premises, employees, decision-making functions, or economic substance; it receives dividends, interest, or royalties from the WFOE and claims the Mainland-Hong Kong DTA's reduced 5% dividend rate and 7% interest/royalty rates solely for tax avoidance while immediately passing funds to an ultimate shareholder in a third jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: EIT Law Article 47 and the General Anti-Avoidance Rules permit the tax authority to make a special tax adjustment and recharacterize the arrangement as an aggressive avoidance manipulation; the under-withheld tax becomes immediately due with interest and a penalty of 50%-500% of the tax avoided; the DTA benefit is denied under the principal purpose test and applicable OECD MLI provisions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the WFOE who knowingly under-withheld by filing a false treaty claim may be jointly and severally liable for the uncollected withholding tax. Persons identified as tax evaders may be added to the serious-honesty-tax-offender list (blacklist), subjected to exit restrictions/travel bans, and if the scheme is executed through fraudulent instruments, criminally prosecuted as accomplices, resulting in personal fines and imprisonment up to seven years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing and Profit Shifting (AI API/LLM Royalty Manipulation)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE sells AI API inference services to a Hong Kong group company at prices below arm's length and purchases LLM technology licences from Hong Kong at excessive royalty rates, concentrating profit in Hong Kong while keeping the Chinese WFOE at breakeven; no contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation is prepared, and the Hong Kong recipient has no R&D personnel or CIGA to justify the royalty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: EIT Law Articles 41, 44, 48 and 49 and SAT Announcement 2016 No. 42 authorize a transfer-pricing primary adjustment, secondary adjustments, interest on the adjusted tax, and penalties of 50%-150% where documentation is deficient or incomplete; the understated income is reallocated to China and the royalty payment is recharacterized as a constructive dividend subject to non-resident withholding tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: If directors caused the WFOE to enter into fictitious or abusive related-party contracts, the corporate veil may be pierced under PRC Company Law (abuse of independent corporate personality causing loss to creditors or tax collection) to seize personal assets; exit restrictions may be imposed for intentional tax evasion; criminal liability under Criminal Law Articles 201 and 203 can result in imprisonment of up to seven years for the responsible legal representative and finance director.
